# A bill posted to a plain liability, naming fund units as its settlement.
#
# The units refusal again, on a book where the record's owner and its posted
# account disagree about what kind of record it is. The owner is a vendor, so
# this is a bill and every sentence built from the owner says so; the posted
# account is `type: Liability` rather than Accounts Payable, so anything
# reading the account's type concludes "not a payable" and reaches for the
# invoice word.
#
# The refusal names the record's own account in the same breath as the word
# "bill", so the two have to come from the same place. Read from the account,
# it says "this bill's own receivable" — a phrase with a contradiction inside
# it, about an account the book has not got.
#
# What this fixture produces: a refusal naming `Assets:Fund`, the bill, and
# the payable.
#
# Verified by
# tests/integration/test_linking_a_split_not_on_the_receivable.py.
bill "BILL-USD-002"
  vendor_id: "V-US"
  currency: USD
  date_opened: 2026-01-05
  entry:
    date: 2026-01-05
    description: "Parts"
    account: "Expenses:Supplies"
    quantity: 1
    price: 100
    taxable: false
  posted:
    date: 2026-01-05
    due: 2026-02-05
    ap_account: "Liabilities:Other Payables"
    memo: "Bill BILL-USD-002"
    accumulate: true
  payment:
    date: 2026-03-30
    amount: 100
    account: "Assets:Bank:USD"
    txn_guid: "2a3b4c5d6e7f8a9b0c5f6a7b8c9d0e1f"
    txn_split_guid: "4c5d6e7f8a9b0c5f6a7b8c9d0e1f2a3b"
